title: Seedframe temporal annotations
content:
Purpose: quick personal log for experimenting with 'seedframes' — tiny curated few-shot sets that include explicit temporal annotations (timestamps, relative order hints) to push model behavior to respect event order and persistence across turns. Goal is to find compact templates that reduce hallucinated time/sequence shifts in short multi-step tasks (FAQ updates, timeline summarization, chat memory sim).

Notes / hypotheses (rough):
- Hypothesis A: embedding explicit ISO timestamps (2024-11-05T14:23Z) in few-shot exemplars reduces temporal drift when prompts ask for 'what happened next' style reasoning.
- Hypothesis B: relative anchors ("Step 1, Step 2") plus small narrativization reduces model reordering at generation time versus raw bullet exemplars.
- Hypothesis C: adding an explicit "as-of" context line at top ("As of 2024-11-05") improves consistency when the model invents future events.

Quick experiment matrix (tracked informally):
- Model v1 (open-7b-quant): temperature 0.2; few-shot=3; exemplar style=A (ISO timestamps). Outcome: fewer reorderings but occasional invented steps beyond last timestamp.
- Model v1: temp 0.0; exemplar style=B (step anchors+narrative). Outcome: more conservative, sometimes repeats prior step text verbatim (overfitting).
- Model v2 (redwood-hosted-ggml): temp 0.2; exemplar style=C (as-of header). Outcome: good suppression of future hallucinations, but truncated completions under 120-token budget.

Representative seedframe template (prototype):
-- CONTEXT: As of 2024-11-05T14:23Z, customer-reported events for Service-X --
EXEMPLAR 1:
  TIME: 2024-10-30T09:15Z
  EVENT: Deployed patch v1.2.3 to canary; observed increased 5xx rate on worker-3.
  ACTION: Rolled back to v1.2.2; Kibana snapshot attached.
EXEMPLAR 2:
  TIME: 2024-10-31T12:40Z
  EVENT: CPU spikes on job-scheduler during bulk import; added temporary rate-limit.
  ACTION: Created follow-up ticket SCHED-457.
PROMPT: Given events above, produce a short timeline (ordered newest->oldest) with one-sentence ramifications for each event.
EXPECTED: keep order consistent with TIME fields; do not invent events beyond 2024-11-05.

Failure cases observed (notes):
- Case F1: Model reorders exemplars when asked to summarize by impact instead of time; loses explicit TIME anchors and sorts by perceived importance.
- Case F2: With very low token budgets (<80 tokens), model truncates the last exemplar and omits the final action. Helps to add "END-OF-EXAMPLAR" token to force closure.
- Case F3: When exemplars use relative terms like "yesterday", model resolves relative terms incorrectly if prompt includes a different 'as-of' date. Best to normalize to ISO or explicitly say "yesterday relative to AS-OF".

Mini-investigations to run next (TODOs):
- [ ] Compare "ISO timestamp" vs "relative phrase + as-of header" across redwood-hosted-2 and open-7b-quant; log token usage. (linked GH PR: GH-PR-7890)
- [ ] Try explicit end-markers around few-shot examples: <EX1>...</EX1>. See if parser helps continuity.
- [ ] Create short eval set (10 items) focusing on: timeline ordering, no-future-invention, and action-preservation. Run nightly for a week.
- [ ] Draft a short Confluence note summarizing promising templates (CONFLUENCE-1234).

Prompt variants tried (snippets):
- Variant A (ISO anchors): "TIME: 2024-10-30T09:15Z — EVENT: ..."
- Variant B (step anchors): "STEP 1: Deployed patch v1.2.3 -> RESULT: 5xx increase"
- Variant C (narrative bullets): "On 2024-10-30, we deployed a patch which caused..."
- Variant D (closed tokens): "<EXAMPLE> ... </EXAMPLE>"

Quick results table (informal):
- Ordering fidelity: B > A > C for v1; C slightly better on v2.
- Invention suppression: C with as-of header best.
- Token overhead: A > B (ISO uses more tokens).

Fieldnotes / heuristics discovered:
- Use step anchors when the user cares about ordinal positions (first/second) rather than absolute timestamps.
- Use ISO anchors when you need cross-doc alignment or machine-parseability.
- As-of header reduces 'future invention' more than any single exemplar tweak.
- Always include a negative instruction low in the prompt: "Do not invent events beyond AS-OF." Works reasonably well as a soft constraint.

Examples of model mis-output to keep as counterexamples (copy raw to confluence later):
- Output A (bad): "After rollback on 2024-10-30 we upgraded to v1.2.4 which fixed it." (invented v1.2.4)
- Output B (bad): "Scheduler outage started on 2024-11-10" (date beyond AS-OF)
- Output C (ok but verbose): repeats full action blocks verbatim — acceptable for fidelity but noisy.

Links / references I want nearby:
- Related Slack thread: #prompt-experiments (thread C7F2), note by Priya on 2024-10-29
- GH PR: GH-PR-7890 (seedframe helper lib — prototype serializer for ISO + step anchors)
- Confluence draft: CONFLUENCE-1234 (seedframe templates)

Loose long-term idea: treat seedframes as tiny structured context units that can be stored and referenced by id (like memory-chunks) so user prompts can refer to 'seedframe:id=xyz as-of=...' and the runtime can enforce as-of checks and canonicalization. This could be a low-overhead memory primitive for retrieval-augmented prompts in the console.

Random note-to-self: when drafting the eval harness, include a synthetic 'noisy exemplar' variant to test robustness to partial/mangled timestamps (missing timezone, day-first vs month-first parsing).

End of notes (for now).
